# Results — Study 903 (Sector-Neutral Low-Vol)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — the
**low-volatility anomaly** (Baker-Bradley-Wurgler 2011; Frazzini-Pedersen 2014): calm stocks
out-earn wild ones risk-adjusted, so a long-low-vol / short-high-vol book earns a positive
spread. The critique tested here: a naive low-vol sort is partly a **defensive-sector** bet;
we strip it by ranking each name's trailing volatility **within its own sector** and asking
whether a genuine stock-level low-vol effect survives. Offline & deterministic once cached;
run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last
complete calendar month; the partial current month is dropped). Fingerprint `357fd262912f`
(panel Close).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily OHLC (`auto_adjust=True`, total-return), **50 liquid US large-caps**, 2010-01-04 → 2026-06-30, **4,147** dated rows/name |
| Universe | a fixed `UNIVERSE` of ~50 mega-caps, pulled through the **`quantlab.universe` survivorship guard** (`download_panel(..., allow_survivorship_bias=True)`), cached under this study's own `_cache/`; each name carries a fixed **GICS sector** label (`SECTORS`) |
| Sectors | InfoTech 14, Financials 7, Industrials 7, ConsDisc 5, CommServices 5, HealthCare 5, Staples 5, Energy 2 (Staples + HealthCare = the 20% "defensive" bucket) |
| Signal | each name's **trailing-63-day realized volatility** (std of daily simple returns), known at the close of `t−1` (one `shift`) |
| Sector demean | on each day, subtract from each name's vol the **cross-sectional median vol of its own sector** (the sector-neutral signal); a raw variant sorts the vol un-demeaned |
| Sort | each day rank the cross-section; **long the bottom 30%** (low vol), **short the top 30%** (high vol), equal-weight; measure the day-`t` forward return of each book |
| Execution / costs | one documented lag: signal through close `t−1` → hold day `t`. The costed timer charges 2 sides × one-way cost × NAV per day; the short (high-vol) book pays 50 bps/yr borrow |
| Statistics | Newey-West (HAC, 10-lag) *t* on the daily spread; one-sample *t*; Welch *t* on the pooled low-vs-high books; per-leg Sharpe race; a defensive-tilt diagnostic; a 1,000-permutation placebo; a 20-seed synthetic positive control |

**Survivorship — named on the Signal axis.** `UNIVERSE` is a **current-membership** list of
names that are liquid mega-caps *today*, so the magnitudes are an **upper bound**. The
low-vol premium is also documented as strongest in small/illiquid names; a 50-mega-cap
survivor panel is exactly where it is *least* likely to appear — which is what we find.

## The headline — raw vs sector-neutral low-vol spread

Daily equal-weight bottom-30% (low vol) minus top-30% (high vol) spread, n = **4,083** days:

| book | spread (low − high) | NW(10) *t* | one-sample *t* | low-vol / high-vol book | Welch *t* | gross Sharpe |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Raw** (sector-tilted) | **−4.74 bps/day** | **−2.61** | −2.47 | +5.21 / +9.95 bps | −1.66 | −0.61 |
| **Sector-neutral** | **−3.53 bps/day** | **−2.67** | −2.52 | +6.54 / +10.08 bps | −1.26 | −0.63 |

The low-vol edge **fails to replicate — and inverts.** The anomaly predicts a *positive*
long-low/short-high spread (calm names out-earn); on this mega-cap universe the spread is
**significantly negative** in both books: the wild **high-vol** names (the tech mega-caps —
NVDA, TSLA, AMD) *out-earned* the calm ones over 2010–2026. Stripping the sector bet moves
the spread by only **+1.20 bps** and leaves it significantly wrong-signed (NW *t* = −2.67).

## The per-leg Sharpe race — the *risk-adjusted* low-vol claim

The anomaly is really about return **per unit of risk**, so race each leg's own (≈
excess-of-cash) annualised Sharpe:

| book | low-vol leg Sharpe (vol) | high-vol leg Sharpe (vol) | verdict |
|---|--:|--:|---|
| **Raw** | **0.98** (0.13) | **0.98** (0.26) | a *tie* — no low-vol advantage |
| **Sector-neutral** | **1.05** (0.16) | **1.07** (0.24) | high-vol leg *edges it* |

Even on its own turf the low-vol leg wins **no** Sharpe advantage: raw it merely ties (same
Sharpe at half the vol — the closest thing to the classic result, but *not* the claimed edge),
and once sector-neutral the high-vol leg is marginally *higher*. There is no stock-level
low-vol premium here to survive.

## The defensive-sector tilt — what the raw sort actually buys

| book | long book % defensive | short book % defensive | long − short | (universe 20.0%) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Raw** | **44.7%** | 5.2% | **+39.5%** | a large defensive-sector bet |
| **Sector-neutral** | 13.9% | 15.7% | **−1.8%** | bet removed |

The naive low-vol sort is, mechanically, **long-defensive / short-cyclical**: its long book is
45% Staples + Health Care versus 20% in the universe. The demean collapses that tilt to zero —
confirming the critique's premise that much of a raw low-vol book *is* a sector bet — but
removing it does not rescue a stock-level edge.

## Placebo — is the (reversed) relation a lucky alignment of the sort?

Keep the sector-neutral trailing-vol sort but read each day's forward returns from a
**column-permuted** panel (signal → outcome link broken), 1,000 permutations (20 seeds × 50):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| observed spread | **−3.53 bps** |
| placebo mean (sd) | −0.005 bps (0.993) |
| position of observed | ≈ **3.55σ into the left tail** (right-tail p = 1.000 ⇒ left-tail p ≈ 0.000) |

The permutation null centres at zero; the observed −3.53 bps sits far in the **left** tail, so
the (opposite-sign) relation is real and not a lucky sort — the sign is simply the reverse of
the literature's on this universe.

## Robustness — two eras (split 2018-01-01, sector-neutral)

| era | spread | NW *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| 2010-01 → 2018-01 (n=1,949) | −3.08 bps | **−1.93** |
| 2018-01 → 2026-06 (n=2,134) | −3.95 bps | **−1.90** |

The reversal is the *same sign* in both halves (each individually just shy of |2|, the full
sample −2.67) — not one era's artefact.

## The timer — can you get paid for it (sector-neutral book)?

Charge 2 sides × one-way × NAV per day on the long-short book; short (high-vol) pays 50 bps/yr borrow.

| one-way cost | gross/day | cost/day | net/day | *t* (net) | Sharpe (net) | ~ann. |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **1 bp** | −3.53 bps | 2.14 bps | **−5.67 bps** | −4.04 | −1.00 | −14.3%/yr |
| **5 bps** | −3.53 bps | 10.14 bps | **−13.67 bps** | −9.74 | −2.42 | −34.4%/yr |

The specified book loses money gross; and even the *sign-flipped* book (long high-vol) would
earn only +3.53 bps/day gross, most of which the 2.14 bps/day round-trip friction at a mere 1
bp one-way already eats. **Mirage** either way.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is sound

Deterministic seeded panel with an explicit sector structure: sectors differ in base vol and
carry a mean **premium correlated with their calmness** (the defensive-sector confound), and —
with `edge>0` — names are cheaper the higher their vol *within their own sector*. No network.

| world | sort | NW *t* |
|---|---|--:|
| null (`edge=0`, no sector premium), **20 seeds** | sector-neutral | mean **+0.20** (sd 0.64), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 0/20** |
| planted within-sector low-vol (`edge=0.1`, seed 903) | sector-neutral | **+4.23** (Welch *t* = +4.35) |
| confound (`edge=0`, **only** a sector premium), 20 seeds | **raw** | mean **+3.46** (fires **18/20**) |
| confound (same worlds) | **sector-neutral** | **0/20** — silent |

The neutral detector recovers a *planted* within-sector low-vol effect cleanly and never fires
on the null; crucially, a pure defensive-**sector** premium fools the **raw** sort (mean *t* =
+3.46) but the demean leaves the **sector-neutral** sort silent — proof the neutralisation
strips the sector bet. So the negative real-tape result is a genuine null, not a bug.
*(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The low-volatility edge does **not** survive on 50 liquid US mega-caps.
  The sector-neutral long-low-vol / short-high-vol spread is **−3.53 bps/day** (NW *t* =
  **−2.67**) — significant but *opposite in sign* to the claim (the wild tech names out-earned),
  holding in both eras (*t* = −1.93 / −1.90), ≈3.55σ into the left tail of a 1,000-permutation
  placebo. On the anomaly's own **Sharpe** axis the low-vol leg wins no advantage once
  sector-neutral (1.05 vs 1.07). What character the *raw* sort had was largely a
  **defensive-sector tilt** (long book 45% defensive; neutralising moved the spread only +1.20
  bps), and the synthetic control confirms the machinery (a pure sector premium fools the raw
  sort at *t* = +3.46, the neutral sort stays silent). Survivorship biases the magnitude.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The sector-neutral book loses money gross and net (−5.67 bps/day at
  1 bp, −13.67 at 5 bps); even the data-mined sign-flip is eaten by the round-trip friction.
